text: Cattle have small lungs relative to their body size (about 12.4 liters lung volume in a cow, compared to 42 liters in a horse), and the lungs sit deep in the chest — this makes cattle prone to respiratory disease, since once viruses or bacteria reach the lungs they can persist and develop infection, and even a small loss of lung capacity from infection is a serious matter. Normal breathing rate is 10–20 movements/minute for an adult and 15–30 movements/minute for a calf.
